## Re-review at `9cd7e890` — both items resolved

**1. `getCached()` evicting the last-known-good fallback — fixed**

The `_sidecarCache.delete(key)` on the stale path is gone. [`getCached`](https://github.com/bradleybond512/crystal-ball/blob/9cd7e8904c6000dd3bf4052c650319dcf5426284/src-tauri/sidecar/local-api-server.mjs#L5300-L5305) and [`getCachedStale`](https://github.com/bradleybond512/crystal-ball/blob/9cd7e8904c6000dd3bf4052c650319dcf5426284/src-tauri/sidecar/local-api-server.mjs#L5306-L5309) are now byte-identical to `main`.

[`_sweepSidecarCache`](https://github.com/bradleybond512/crystal-ball/blob/9cd7e8904c6000dd3bf4052c650319dcf5426284/src-tauri/sidecar/local-api-server.mjs#L5284-L5291) actually goes further than base: it no longer reaps TTL-expired entries at all, only trimming oldest-first above the cap. So expired entries now survive as fallbacks by design rather than incidentally. `SIDECAR_CACHE_MAX = 500` is unchanged, so memory stays bounded.

Re-ran the repro against the new head — the `getCachedStale()` call sites (GDACS, NSIDC, IPAWS, …) recover last-known-good data when upstream fails:

```
64b9e16c   fresh=null   stale=null
9cd7e890   fresh=null   stale={"events":["REAL LAST-KNOWN-GOOD"]}
```

**2. `usgs-surface-water` snapshot binding — fixed**

[`feed-catalog.ts:126`](https://github.com/bradleybond512/crystal-ball/blob/9cd7e8904c6000dd3bf4052c650319dcf5426284/src/services/diagnostics/feed-catalog.ts#L124-L126) now carries `sidecarKey: 'usgs-surface-water'` (no collision with the existing `sidecarKey: 'usgs'` earthquakes entry), and the route records fail-closed telemetry derived from adapter output rather than HTTP status — `recordFeedSuccess` only when `result.features.length > 0`, `recordFeedFailure(..., 'no_contributed_rows')` otherwise. That's the right shape: a 200 with zero contributed rows won't cast a phantom healthy vote.

**Tests** — run locally at `9cd7e890`: `sidecar-ttl-cache-guards` 15 pass / 0 fail, `feed-health-panel` + `feed-catalog` 34 pass / 0 fail. The two added regression tests cover both directions (expired data preserved for fallback, oldest still evicted above the hard cap).

**Nit, non-blocking:** `_ensureSidecarCacheSweep` still arms a 5-minute interval, but `_sweepSidecarCache` is now a no-op below the cap, and `setCached` already invokes it on exactly that condition. The timer is effectively dead weight — harmless, since it's `unref`'d.

No further blocking findings.
